article_text:
Eva Marie Saint war einer der letzten weiblichen Stars, die in der „Goldenen Ära“ Hollywoods groß geworden sind; im Alter von 102 Jahren ist die US-amerikanische Schauspielerin am 6. Oktober 2026 in Los Angeles verstorben. Im kollektiven Filmgedächtnis bleibt sie nicht zuletzt durch ihren ikonischen Auftritt in Alfred Hitchcocks „Der unsichtbare Dritte“.

Mit Eva Marie Saint ist am 6. Oktober 2026 eine der letzten US-Schauspielerinnen verstorben, die im Hollywoodkino der „Goldenen Ära“ groß wurden. Ihren ersten „Oscar“ gewann die 1924 in New Jersey geborene US-Amerikanerin, die zunächst als Theaterdarstellerin in Erscheinung trat, gleich für ihren ersten Kinoauftritt in „ Die Faust im Nacken “: für die Nebenrolle als „love interest“ von Marlon Brando. Ein anrührend-eindringlicher Part, der schon am Beginn ihrer Leinwandkarriere bewies, dass Eva Marie Saint nicht nur über klassische Schönheit, sondern auch über das Zeug zur Charakterdarstellerin verfügte. Ins kollektive Kinogedächtnis schrieb sie sich vor allem mit ihrem Part als mysteriöse Blondine in Alfred Hitchcocks Spionage-Thriller „ Der unsichtbare Dritte “ (1959) ein. Der große Showdown, in dem ihre Figur Eve Kendall an der Seite von Cary Grant vor den Bösewichtern fliehen muss, in rotem Kostüm, weißen Handschuhen und High Heels am Mount Rushmore baumelt und dabei noch die Luft hat zu flirten, gehört in seiner Mischung aus Spannung und Romantik zu den ikonischsten Szenen des Genres.

Bis in die 1960er-Jahre arbeitete Eva Marie Saint mit vielen wichtigen Regisseuren wie Otto Preminger („Exodus“) und Vincente Minnelli („Die alles begehren“, 1965) zusammen; den Nimbus der großen weiblichen Stars jener Ära erreichte sie aber nie. „Eva Marie Saint hätte es mit ihrem Talent in den Olymp der Hollywood-Stars schaffen können“, schrieb Michael Ranze in einem Porträt anlässlich des 100. Geburtstags der Schauspielerin, „doch wegen der mangelnden Qualitäten der Drehbücher machte sie sich rar und nahm nur ausgewählte Rollen an, wodurch sie letztlich im Schatten von Diven wie Elizabeth Taylor, Marilyn Monroe oder Grace Kelly blieb.“ Auch privat suchte Saint nie forciert das Rampenlicht. Von 1951 an war sie mit dem zwei Jahre jüngeren Regisseur und Produzenten Jeffrey Hayden verheiratet und blieb bis zu dessen Tod im Jahr 2016 mit ihm zusammen.

In den 1970er-Jahren zog sich Eva Marie Saint weitgehend aus dem Kino zurück und arbeitete wieder mehr auf der Theaterbühne oder auch fürs Fernsehen. Bis in die 2010er-Jahre war sie zumindest vereinzelt in Kinofilmen zu sehen. Einer ihrer letzten und zugleich schönsten Leinwandauftritte war 2005 die Rolle der Mutter der von Sam Shepard verkörperten Hauptfigur in Wim Wenders’ „ Don’t Come Knocking “, eine ebenso herbe wie liebenswerte Altersrolle. Am 6. Oktober 2026 ist Eva Marie Saint im stolzen Alter von 102 Jahren im Kreis ihrer Familie in Los Angeles verstorben.

article_text:
Anthony Ippolito had to do more than nail Sylvester Stallone’s signature voice to play him in “ I Play Rocky .”

He also had to transform his skinny physique to one with bulging muscles.

“It had its moments for sure. I was being tested,” Ippolito told me Saturday at the AFI Fest “I Play Rocky” screening in Los Angeles. “It’s like a consistency thing, though. I had a great deal of time, so just an entire lifestyle shift and it was just one of the priorities of every day for a pretty long period.”

Related Stories

Music Industry Moves: Believe Names Adriana Sein President of Americas; Guy Moot Joins NMPA Board

Met and interviewed ‘I Play Rocky’ star Anthony Ippolito for the first time today. We talked about the muscles he put on to transform into Sylvester Stallone and acting opposite a dog playing Butkus. https://t.co/rd2mkN8lBD via @variety #justforvariety pic.twitter.com/yCnvV4IWM9 — Marc Malkin (@marcmalkin) October 25, 2026

As Ippolito previously told Variety ’s Clayton Davis, he spent nearly two years bulking up from about 150 pounds to roughly 180 while training at Gleason’s Gym in Brooklyn.

What did family and friends think?

“It happened over time, but a couple of people were like, ‘What’s going on?’” Ippolito recalled. “They didn’t necessarily know I was doing the prep, and they were like, ‘What’s going on here?’ I was like, ‘I’ve been going to the gym, been eating.’”

“I Play Rocky,” directed by Peter Farrelly, follows Stallone’s journey to get “Rocky” made in 1976. Now considered one of the greatest films ever made, the odds were way more against Stallone than with him when he first pitched the movie in Hollywood.

AnnaSophia Robb plays Stallone’s first wife, Sasha, in “I Play Rocky.” Stephan James portrays Carl Weathers. Rounding out the cast are Kiki Seto, P.J. Byrne, Matt Dillon, Tracy Letts and Jay Duplass.

If jitters on the first day of filming weren’t already enough to contend with, Ippolito’s first scenes were with a dog playing Stallone’s pooch Butkus. Stallone famously sold Butkus for $40 when before he found fame because he couldn’t afford to feed him. After selling the “Rocky” script, he bought him back for $15,000.

Anthony Ippolito describes his first day filming "I Play Rocky": "Irwin Winkler was actually on set day one. We did a lot of stuff with Butkus that day, and I hadn't met that specific dog until the day prior to shooting, and he didn't happen to take a liking to me until a… pic.twitter.com/7tPKpNnp4M — Variety (@Variety) October 24, 2026

“I hadn’t met that specific dog until like the day prior to shooting,” Ippolito said. “He didn’t happen to take a liking to me until a couple of days in. When you give him enough treats, then he started to warm up. But at that point he was, you know, a 140-, 160-pound dog [and] wasn’t a huge fan of me, so it kind of just added to it. He just did whatever he wanted to do, and that was usually not what we were looking for him to do … In some ways they, they give you the most beautiful stuff. It’s just you gotta be patient.”

“I Play Rocky” is in limited release on Nov. 6, followed by going wide on Nov. 20.

See more photos from the “I Play Rocky” screening at AFI Fest below.

長谷川 繁 ペイン天狗 2026年10月24日（土）–2027年1月24日（日） 豊田市美術館 展示室1–5 https://www.museum.toyota.aichi.jp/ 開館時間：10:00–17:30（入場は閉館30分前まで） 休館日：月（ただし、11/23、1/11は開館）、12/28–1/4 企画担当：千葉真智子（豊田市美術館学芸員）、都筑正敏（豊田市美術館学芸員） 展覧会URL： https://www.museum.toyota.aichi.jp/exhibition/hasegawa2026

豊田市美術館では、画家・長谷川繁の長年の制作を新旧織り交ぜながら紹介する個展「長谷川 繁 ペイン天狗」を開催する。 長谷川繁 （1963年生まれ）は、愛知県立芸術大学大学院を修了後、1989年にドイツに渡り、デュッセルドルフ芸術アカデミーでヤン・ディベッツに学んだ。1992年にオランダに移り、アムステルダムのデ・アトリエーズでのレジデンスを経て、1996年まで同地に滞在した。ナスやキュウリ、バナナ、魚といった静物画を思わせるモチーフや、ドレープや椅子の脚など西洋由来のモチーフを、意味を剥ぎ取られた形として組み合わせ、限られた要素で常に違う絵を描こうと試みてきた。2013年に発表を休止したが、その間も制作は続けられ、2019年に個展を再開して以降、精力的に作品を発表している。近年の主な展覧会に、個展「金金金生光」（Satoko Oe Contemporary、東京、2025）、特集展示「MOTコレクション Eye to Eye—見ること」（東京都現代美術館、2024）、二人展「ペイン天狗とホト愚裸夫」（See Saw gallery+hibit、愛知、2024）、個展「1989-」（横浜市民ギャラリーあざみ野、神奈川、2023）、個展「SCARECROW」（Satoko Oe Contemporary、東京、2023）、二人展「ペイン天狗」（カスヤの森現代美術館、神奈川、2022）、個展「painting」（Nonaka-Hill、ロサンゼルス、2022）などがある。

本展では、油彩画約120点のほか、ドローイングや資料などを展示する。最初の吹き抜けの部屋では、新旧、大小の作品を織り交ぜ、長谷川の制作の飛躍的な展開と一貫性とが体感できる。なかには、およそ30年ぶりに手がけた3メートル超の大作3点も含まれる。1989年からおよそ3年半におよぶドイツ留学時代については、帰国後長らく開梱せずに留めておいた未発表作の油彩画などをまとめて紹介する。続く、オランダ時代の絵画としては、3メートルを超す山口県立美術館の所蔵作品3点を中心に展示。長谷川にとってブレイクスルーとなった「生姜」をモチーフにした作品もある。 長谷川は作品を展示する空間についても自問してきた。西洋の模倣、まがいもの文化に囲まれて生活してきたと述べる長谷川にとって、キッチュな壁紙に覆われた部屋はそれに相応しいものに感じられるという。展示室3では、長谷川デザインによるオリジナルの壁紙を背に、40点ほどの小品を全面に展示。さらに展示室5では、既製品の壁紙を背にルネ・マグリットやウィリアム・モリス、会田誠など、長谷川が選んだ豊田市美術館の所蔵作品と共に、長谷川の作品を展示する。あわせて、ガラスケース内で作家の雑多な蒐集品やドローイングを紹介する。

"在其策展序言中，孔蒂将水女性主义思想提炼为展览的概念核心。这一视角交汇于女性主义研究、后人类主义和政治生态学之间，对人类作为独立于环境的自主个体的观念提出了质疑。作为该理论的主要代表人物之一阿斯特里达·内马尼斯（Astrida Neimanis）提出，仅仅承认水对生命不可或缺是远远不够的：我们本身就是水之身体，是通过与其他生命及自然周期的物质交换而得以生存的多孔有机体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，这种相互依存关系并非脱离于父权制和殖民统治结构，正是这些结构制约着身体与生态系统的生命状态。并非所有身体和领土都面临着相同的条件。水的获取、污染、私有化或分流，都取决于政治和经济决策，而这些决策的影响分布却是不平等的。熟悉并关心生态系统的社区并不总是有权决定其未来，而那些从其开发中受益的人也不一定是承受其后果的人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从水的角度思考，意味着既要关注维持生命的各种过程，也要关注中断、剥削或危及这些过程的各种结构。在《水之口》中，这种张力通过多种形式得以表现：从渔民社区的知识、水坝建设对河流的改造，到水的精神观念以及捍卫水的集体行动。每件作品都从扎根于具有特定历史和条件的领土的实践与知识出发，来探讨这些问题。", "translated": true}, {"type": Caycedo），《多重阴蒂》（2016）与《蛇河之书》（2017）。“水之口”展览现场，莱斯库埃拉画廊，大西洋大学，哥伦比亚巴兰基亚，2026年。摄影：迭戈·因西尼亚雷斯（Diego Insignares）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卡罗琳娜·凯塞多呈现了其最具代表性的作品之一——《蛇河之书》（2017）。这是一部艺术家书籍，也是其规模更大的研究项目《挡水》（Be Dammed）的一部分，该项目重点关注为截留和调控水流而修建的基础设施（如水坝和运河）对河流生态系统及沿岸居民所产生的影响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该作品以美洲原住民抄本和柏林墙地图为参考，将哥伦比亚、巴西和墨西哥的河流与社区的档案照片、地理地图、卫星图像、诗歌以及艺术家的文本结合在一起。全书共分五章，探讨了理解和栖居河流的各种方式，从河流的神圣属性及其维持的生态平衡，到对河水进行殖民、企业和新殖民式掠夺的形式。书中还审视了无节制开发对环境造成的影响，并汇集了受这些干预措施影响的社区的故事，以及他们对共同财产的抵御和捍卫策略。其蜿蜒的结构令人联想起河流的流向，这一旅程将控制性基础设施与捍卫这些领土的人们的记忆和斗争形成了对照。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在取材自伊瓜苏瀑布的照片拼贴作品《恶性》（Maligna）和《多重阴蒂》（2016）中，卡罗琳娜·凯塞多运用了倒影、对称以及数字和物理重组，将瀑布转化为唤起人体解剖结构的有机形态。在《多重阴蒂》中，“魔鬼咽喉”（Garganta del Diablo）的影像被复制并重叠，直至将急流的力量转化为指向女性生殖器官的形态。通过以身体和女性主义的肖像学来命名这些作品，凯塞多将人体与水体拉近，摆脱了将河流或瀑布仅仅视为自然资源的观念，将其展现为具有超越其开采价值的生命存在的实体。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "水体与人体的关系在塞巴·卡尔夫克奥（Seba Calfuqueo）的录像作品《Kowkülen》（2020）中采取了另一种形式。在第一个场景中，这位马普切艺术家背对镜头，完全浸没在瓦尔马普（Wallmapu）的一条河流中。随后，其赤裸的身体通过绳索悬挂在一棵树上，水流擦过皮肤。我们听到水流淌的声音，而一段在马普切语（mapudungun）和西班牙语之间切换的文本则对西方殖民强加的二元分类提出了质疑。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该作品让人联想起马普切人的领土观念，即不将人类生命与其他存在形式割裂开来，这体现在“itrofil mongen”（意指所有生命的形式）这一概念中。在领土被剥夺、森林单一种林和水资源开发的大背景下，这种观点具有了政治维度。与将水视为商品的观念相对，卡尔夫克奥将其呈现为一个活生生的神圣实体。身体和语言的流动性反过来主张了一种非二元的栖居和理解世界的方式，其中性别、记忆、领土和自然并不构成孤立的领域。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": aq’（夜幕降临）》。展出于哥伦比亚巴兰基亚大西洋大学莱斯库埃拉画廊的“水之口”展览现场，2026年。摄影：迭戈·因西尼亚雷斯", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "水也保存着记忆", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "危地马拉是一个拥有众多河流、湖泊和湿地的国家，但同时也充斥着关于水资源获取、使用和控制的冲突。展览中危地马拉艺术家的出现，从这一背景引入了领土剥夺、污染以及生态系统保护的历史，这些历史与哥伦比亚的现实产生了共鸣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在录像作品《Qatee ya’ [祖母湖]》（2024）中，圣佩德罗拉拉古纳（San Pedro La Laguna）的玛雅茨图吉尔族（Maya Tz’utujil）艺术家切恩（Cheen）和曼努埃尔·查瓦哈伊（Manuel Chavajay）从一个与阿蒂特兰湖相关的梦境出发。该作品重现了切恩的叙述，他在梦中收到了来自“祖母湖”（玛雅茨图吉尔族宇宙观中的精神存在）的信息。从这一角度来看，该湖不仅是生计来源或旅游目的地，更是一个需要关怀、倾听和责任的生命。梦境与口头叙事传递着这样的知识：精神与生态构成了对领土的同一愿景，并指导着社区与其水域的关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曼努埃尔·查瓦哈伊在两幅画作中探讨了阿蒂特兰湖的污染问题，画作中融入了船用和汽车发动机的废机油，这种残留物凸显了旅游业和日常航行对环境产生的影响。艺术家将其描述为“自然的血液”，当人类的贪婪和野心划破大地时，它便涌流而出。机油的物质融合使对湖泊造成的破坏变得显而易见，并将污染转化为了环境暴力的图像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "玛雅卡克奇克尔族（Maya Kaqchikel）艺术家玛丽莲·博尔·博（Marilyn Boror Bor）通过其他材料审视了领地剥夺问题。《夺走了我们的水，我们在水泥上涂满蓝色来记住它 I》（2026）是一件由水泥块组成的壁画装置，水泥块中包裹着染有绿色和群青色颜料的丝线。水泥暗喻了一种掩盖并改变大地的进步模式；蓝色则让人联想到水以及玛雅蓝的文化传统。被困在块体中的丝线暗示了一条被禁锢的河流，其缺席却在记忆中挥之不去。这件作品与圣胡安萨卡特佩克斯（San Juan Sacatepéquez）的冲突有关，在那里，水泥工业的扩张对当地领地造成了负面影响，并引发了社区抗议。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Riosdegente_Foto_Juan-Esteban.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "雷吉娜·何塞·加林多（Regina José Galindo）作品《人群之河》（2021）。图：胡安·埃斯特班（Juan Esteban）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在雷吉娜·何塞·加林多（Regina José Galindo）的作品《人群之河》（2021）中，为水的抗争具有了集体规模。该作品与原住民维权人士阿韦利诺·丘布·卡尔（Abelino Chub Caal）共同构思，记录了一场行动：来自危地马拉受采矿、水力发电项目、单一作物种植和污染影响的社区的千余名民众，走过那些河流曾被改道或变得无法接近的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "参与者们手持一幅长长的半透明蓝色织物，它代表着一条流淌的河床。随着他们如同一股人类洪流般向前推进，他们让那些因过度开发、污染和通行限制而受损的水流重现于世。这一行动将对这些河流的象征性夺回，转化为对水作为公共资源的集体诉求。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Guanaquilla-Luminosa.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "索菲亚·加利萨·穆里恩特，《Guaniquilla luminosa》，2023。数字视频，采用苏打8毫米胶片经胡尤亚山区的水手工冲洗，5’02’’。艺术家供图", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "水也能产生影像", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《发光的瓜尼基利亚》（2023）中，索菲娅·加利萨·穆里恩特（Sofía Gallisá Muriente）用超8毫米（Super 8）胶片拍摄了波多黎各卡沃罗霍（Cabo Rojo）的瓜尼基利亚（Guaniquilla）泻湖，并用哈尤亚山脉的水手工冲洗胶片。水中的矿物质、藻类和其他颗粒物改变了乳剂，在影像上留下了斑点和不规则痕迹。这一过程将该岛的两个领地及其各自的历史联系在了一起：瓜尼基利亚的森林保护区保留了西班牙殖民时期一座古代甘蔗庄园的痕迹，并正在经历生态恢复过程；而哈尤亚则是中部山区以原住民考古遗址闻名的一个地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该胶片是长期项目《泻湖天文台》（Observatorio de lagunas）的一部分，该项目旨在探究记忆及其空白。标题既指代受潮汐涨落影响的海岸生态系统，也指代标志着回忆的种种缺席。水在胶片上留下的痕迹使这种环境与记录和铭记的方式（永远是局部的）之间的关系具象化了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "特立尼达艺术家娜迪亚·霍金斯（Nadia Huggins）通过摄影双联画系列《转型》（Transformations，2014-2015）探讨了对海洋生态系统中身体的感知。该项目源于她日常的游泳、对珊瑚礁退化的担忧，以及她在潜入水中时体验到的失重感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "每幅双联画将一张艺术家身体的照片与一张海洋动物的照片并置。两者之间留下了一个似乎即将消失的间隙，仿佛两张照片可以融为一体。转型发生在将它们分隔又同时使它们接近的空间中。目光在那里摇摆不定，既在分辨这两个世界，又将它们感知为同一连续体的一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BOCAS-DE-AGUA-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "娜迪亚·霍金斯，《转型》（Transformations，2014-2015）。“水的诸口”（Bocas de agua）展览现场，拉埃斯库拉画廊，大西洋大学，哥伦比亚巴兰基亚，2026。图：迭戈·因西尼亚雷斯（Diego Insignares）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "河流冲刷并带回的物质保留着其旅程的印记。在《我们曾有灰烬之口》（teníamos bocas de ceniza，2026）中，哥伦比亚艺术家玛丽亚·莱吉萨莫（María Leguízamo）从蓬塔罗卡（Punta Roca）的一场集体行动切入，马格达雷纳河在那里沉积了树干、树根、树枝以及人类和工业来源的废弃物。通过对话和对这些材料的观察，她邀请人们将其收集并转移到展厅中，其堆积的形态让人联想到干涸的河床。被侵蚀的木材和其他残余物不仅呈现了塑造其形态的力量——水流、沉积物、震动和时间的流逝——也呈现了人类、工业和掠夺性活动的影响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克里斯蒂安·萨拉布兰卡·迪亚斯（Christian Salablanca Díaz，哥斯达黎加，1990）在《给一条河卸口》（Desbocar un río，2023）中借助了记忆与口头传统，该作品是项目《河流百科全书（液体历史）》（Enciclopedias de Río [Historias Líquidas]）的一部分。这件作品汇集了在河流与海岸考察期间分享的知识，其中包括艺术家从父亲那里听到的关于鱼类、红树林、独木舟和捕鱼实践的故事。在这里，了解一条河流意味着去走近它、观察其生命形式并向那些与它共存的人学习。这些知识诞生于经验，并代代相传。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BOCAS-DE-AGUA-6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "达维·德·热苏斯·多·纳斯西门托（davi de jesus do nascimento）的作品，展于“水的诸口”（Bocas de agua）展览，拉埃斯库拉画廊，大西洋大学，哥伦比亚巴兰基亚，2026。图：迭戈·因西尼亚雷斯（Diego Insignares）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "水的共性（Lo hidrocomún）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "孔蒂的策展为从加勒比地区、中美洲和南美洲社区的宇宙观和经验中理解水的活力提供了多个切入点。“水的诸口”中汇集的艺术作品从具体的情境经验和知识出发，探讨了人类身体与生态系统之间的相互依存关系，承认水是知识生产中的活跃存在，并理解水的退化危及了人类和非人类的生存方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Bocas de agua》还邀请人们思考“水公地”（lo hidrocomún）：认识到水的存在与守护支撑着相互依存的生活方式，然而与之相关的责任和决策权却分布不均。将其视为一种公共财富，既需要关注那些令其得到守护的关系，也需要关注那些制约其获取和开发的政治与经济结构。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览的标题因此超越了作为地理实体的“河口”的含义。河口（boca）是水、空气、言语和故事流通的开口；是不同水流汇聚并发生转化的交汇点。作为 OtherNetwork 接力项目的一部分，该展览在不同地点与社群之间流通着历史与知识，同时并未抹去每个语境的特殊性。正如孔蒂所建议的那样，与水一同思考并不意味着代其发言，而是去关注那些与水共存的生命、记忆和知识形式，以及这种相互依存所带来的责任。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "BOCAS DE AGUA", "links": [{"text": "BOCAS DE AGUA", "url": "https://othernetwork.io/productions/bocas-de-agua/spanish"}], "translated": true}, Leguízamo）、布雷迪·马内斯·罗布莱多（Breidy Manes Robledo）、Nomasmetaforas、克里斯蒂安·萨拉布兰卡·迪亚斯（Christian Salablanca Díaz）合作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉埃斯库拉画廊（Galería La "2026年10月15日至11月12日", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本展览契合 OtherNetwork 促进独立艺术空间之间跨国合作的使命。继在斯图加特、阿克拉、约翰内斯堡、萨尔瓦多和圣胡安举办各届展览之后——每一届都对巡回展览的常规形式进行了检验，“Bocas de article_text:
Bocas de agua reúne en Barranquilla obras que examinan las transformaciones de los ecosistemas acuáticos de América Latina y el Caribe y sus consecuencias para las comunidades: desde el archivo de los pescadores de la Ciénaga de Mallorquín hasta la contaminación del lago Atitlán y las luchas contra proyectos extractivos en Guatemala y Colombia. Bajo la curaduría de Ilaria Conti, de La Nueva Fábrica, la muestra propone otras maneras de entender la convivencia entre los cuerpos humanos y los cuerpos de agua.

La exposición forma parte del programa relay de OtherNetwork , que conecta espacios artísticos independientes de distintas partes del mundo mediante una cadena de proyectos curatoriales en la que cada anfitrión invita al siguiente a trabajar desde su propio contexto. En esta sexta edición, La Casa de Meira , centro de artes y experimentación de Barranquilla, convocó a La Nueva Fábrica , organización independiente con sede en Antigua Guatemala, a desarrollar una muestra curada por su directora ejecutiva y curadora en jefe, Ilaria Conti . Coproducida por OtherNetwork e ifa – Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen , la exposición se presenta en la Galería La Escuela , ubicada en el campus de arte de la Universidad del Atlántico , y reúne obras de artistas de Colombia, Guatemala, Puerto Rico, Costa Rica, Brasil, Trinidad y Tobago y Chile.

En su texto curatorial, Conti propone el pensamiento hidrofeminista como eje conceptual de la muestra. Esta perspectiva, situada en el cruce entre los estudios feministas, el posthumanismo y la ecología política, cuestiona la idea del ser humano como individuo autónomo y separado de su entorno. Astrida Neimanis , una de sus principales exponentes, plantea que no basta con reconocer que el agua es indispensable para la vida: somos cuerpos de agua, organismos porosos cuya existencia depende de intercambios materiales con otros seres y con los ciclos naturales.

Esta interdependencia, sin embargo, no está al margen de las estructuras de dominación patriarcal y colonial, que condicionan tanto la vida de los cuerpos como la de los ecosistemas. No todos los cuerpos y territorios están expuestos a las mismas condiciones. El acceso al agua, su contaminación, privatización o desvío responden a decisiones políticas y económicas cuyos efectos se distribuyen de manera desigual. Las comunidades que conocen y cuidan un ecosistema no siempre tienen poder para decidir sobre su futuro, y quienes se benefician de su explotación tampoco son necesariamente quienes padecen sus consecuencias.

Pensar desde el agua supone atender tanto a los procesos que sostienen la vida como a las estructuras que los interrumpen, los explotan o los ponen en riesgo. En Bocas de agua , esta tensión se expresa en registros diversos, desde los conocimientos de las comunidades pesqueras y la transformación de los ríos por la construcción de represas hasta las concepciones espirituales del agua y las acciones colectivas para defenderla. Cada obra se aproxima a estas cuestiones desde haceres y conocimientos arraigados en territorios con historias y condiciones particulares.

Un territorio hecho de agua

Barranquilla se sitúa en la desembocadura del río Magdalena, allí donde el curso fluvial alcanza el mar Caribe. La geografía de la región responde tanto a los ciclos de los ecosistemas acuáticos como a las intervenciones humanas que modifican sus cauces y alteran la vida de las comunidades que los habitan.

El trabajo conjunto del artista Luis González Vergara y ASOPLAYA , la Asociación de Pescadores del Corregimiento de La Playa , parte de la vida cotidiana de una comunidad que depende de la pesca y el turismo ecológico. La asociación impulsa iniciativas de turismo comunitario e incorpora a mujeres cabeza de hogar a través de la gastronomía, ampliando las formas de participación y sustento vinculadas al entorno.

Manos en el agua (1991-2026), un archivo fotográfico en proceso, reúne fotografías recuperadas en la sede de ASOPLAYA, escaneadas y restauradas, junto con entrevistas a los pescadores Luis Ávila y Leonardo Barranco . Las imágenes muestran a quienes han trabajado durante décadas en la Ciénaga de Mallorquín y han contribuido a recuperar este ecosistema. Las entrevistas recogen relatos transmitidos de voz en voz entre sus habitantes y reconstruyen las historias que acompañan esas imágenes. El archivo incorpora al espacio expositivo una memoria comunitaria y saberes forjados en el trabajo cotidiano con el humedal.

En diálogo con el archivo se presentan cuatro videos de Aproximaciones , serie en la que González Vergara lleva su cuerpo a distintos espacios de la ciénaga y ensaya movimientos para orientarse y mantener el equilibrio sobre superficies inestables. En uno de ellos, realizado junto al pescador Omar Jiménez en la Ciénaga Grande de Santa Marta, el artista explora corporalmente un entorno que Jiménez conoce desde su experiencia en el agua. La serie propone así dos maneras de aproximarse al paisaje: desde el trabajo sostenido de una comunidad arraigada al territorio y desde la exploración corporal de quien busca conocerlo a través de su propia presencia. En ambas, el saber se construye mediante el contacto directo con el agua y la permanencia en el entorno.

Carolina Caycedo presenta una de sus piezas más emblemáticas, Libro Río Serpiente (2017), un libro de artista que forma parte de Be Dammed , un proyecto de investigación más amplio centrado en las consecuencias de las infraestructuras construidas para contener y regular los cursos de agua, como represas y canales, tanto sobre los ecosistemas fluviales como sobre las poblaciones ribereñas.

La obra toma como referencias los códices indígenas de las Américas y los mapas del Muro de Berlín, y combina fotografías de archivo de ríos y comunidades de Colombia, Brasil y México, mapas geográficos, imágenes satelitales, poemas y textos de la artista. Organizado en cinco capítulos, el libro recorre distintas maneras de entender y habitar los ríos, desde su carácter sagrado y los equilibrios ecológicos que sostienen, hasta las formas coloniales, corporativas y neocoloniales de apropiación de sus aguas. También examina los efectos ambientales de la explotación descontrolada y reúne historias de comunidades afectadas por estas intervenciones, junto con sus estrategias de resistencia y defensa de los bienes comunes. Su estructura sinuosa evoca el curso de un río, un recorrido que contrapone las infraestructuras de control con las memorias y luchas de quienes defienden estos territorios.

En los fotocollages Maligna y Clítoris múltiple (2016), realizados a partir de fotografías de las cataratas del Iguazú, Carolina Caycedo recurre al reflejo, la simetría y la recomposición digital y física para transformar las caídas de agua en figuras orgánicas que evocan la anatomía humana. En Clítoris múltiple , las imágenes de la Garganta del Diablo se duplican y superponen hasta convertir la fuerza del torrente en una forma que remite al órgano sexual femenino. Al nombrar estas piezas desde una iconografía corporal y feminista, Caycedo aproxima los cuerpos humanos y los cuerpos de agua, y se aparta de una concepción del río o la cascada como mero recurso natural para presentarlos como entidades vivas, dotadas de una presencia que excede su explotación.

La relación entre cuerpo de agua y cuerpo humano adopta otra forma en el video Kowkülen (2020), de Seba Calfuqueo . En una primera escena, la artista mapuche aparece completamente sumergida en un río del Wallmapu, de espaldas a la cámara. Luego, su cuerpo desnudo cuelga de un árbol mediante amarres, el agua rozando su piel. Escuchamos el fluir del agua, mientras un texto que alterna entre mapudungun y español cuestiona las categorías binarias impuestas por la colonización occidental.

La obra remite a una concepción mapuche del territorio que no separa la vida humana de las demás formas de existencia, expresada en la noción de itrofil mongen . Esta perspectiva adquiere una dimensión política en un contexto de despojo territorial, monocultivos forestales y explotación de los recursos hídricos. Frente a la concepción del agua como mercancía, Calfuqueo la presenta como una entidad viva y sagrada. La fluidez del cuerpo y del lenguaje reivindican, a su vez, formas no binarias de habitar y comprender el mundo, en las que género, memoria, territorio y naturaleza no constituyen ámbitos separados.

Las aguas también guardan memoria

Guatemala es un país de ríos, lagos y humedales, pero también de conflictos por el acceso, el uso y el control del agua. La presencia de artistas guatemaltecos en la muestra introduce, desde este contexto, historias de desposesión territorial, contaminación y defensa de los ecosistemas que encuentran resonancias en la realidad colombiana.

En el video Qatee ya’ [Abuela Lago] (2024), Cheen y Manuel Chavajay , artistas maya tz’utujil de San Pedro La Laguna, parten de un sueño relacionado con el lago Atitlán. La pieza recupera el relato de Cheen, quien recibe durante el sueño un mensaje de la Abuela Lago, presencia espiritual de la cosmovisión maya tz’utujil. Desde esta perspectiva, el lago no es únicamente una fuente de sustento o un destino turístico, sino un ser vivo que demanda cuidado, escucha y responsabilidad. El sueño y la narración oral transmiten saberes en los que lo espiritual y lo ecológico forman parte de una misma visión del territorio, y orientan la relación de la comunidad con sus aguas.

Manuel Chavajay aborda la contaminación del Atitlán en dos pinturas que incorporan aceite quemado de motores marinos y automotrices, un residuo que evidencia los efectos del turismo y de la navegación cotidiana sobre el entorno. El artista lo describe como la sangre de la naturaleza , que brota cuando la avaricia y la ambición humanas abren sus entrañas. La incorporación material del aceite hace visible el daño infligido al lago y convierte la contaminación en una imagen de violencia ambiental.

La artista maya kaqchikel Marilyn Boror Bor examina el despojo territorial mediante otros materiales. Nos quitaron el agua y pintamos de azul el cemento para recordarla I (2026) es una instalación mural compuesta por bloques de cemento que encapsulan hilos de seda teñidos con pigmentos verde y ultramarino. El cemento alude a un modelo de progreso que cubre y altera la tierra; el azul remite al agua y a la tradición cultural del azul maya. Atrapados en los bloques, los hilos sugieren una corriente inmovilizada, cuya ausencia persiste en la memoria. La pieza guarda relación con los conflictos de San Juan Sacatepéquez, donde la expansión de la industria cementera ha impactado negativamente el territorio y provocado movilizaciones comunitarias.

La lucha por el agua cobra una escala colectiva en Ríos de gente (2021), de Regina José Galindo . Concebida junto al defensor indígena Abelino Chub Caal , la obra documenta una acción en la que más de mil personas de comunidades guatemaltecas afectadas por la minería, los proyectos hidroeléctricos, los monocultivos y la contaminación recorrieron lugares donde los ríos habían sido desviados o se habían vuelto inaccesibles.

Los participantes sostuvieron una larga tela translúcida azul que representaba el cauce de un río en movimiento. Al avanzar como una corriente humana, hicieron visibles los cursos de agua afectados por la explotación, la contaminación y las restricciones de acceso. La acción convirtió la recuperación simbólica de esos ríos en una reivindicación colectiva del agua como bien común.

El agua también produce imágenes

En Guaniquilla luminosa (2023), Sofía Gallisá Muriente filma en Super 8 la laguna Guaniquilla, en Cabo Rojo, Puerto Rico, y revela la película a mano con agua de las montañas de Jayuya. Los minerales, las algas y otras partículas presentes en el agua alteran la emulsión y dejan manchas e irregularidades en las imágenes. Este procedimiento pone en relación dos territorios de la isla y sus respectivas historias: Guaniquilla, donde una reserva forestal conserva la huella de una antigua hacienda cañera del período colonial español y atraviesa un proceso de recuperación ecológica, y Jayuya, localidad de las montañas centrales conocida por sus sitios arqueológicos indígenas.

La película forma parte de Observatorio de lagunas, un proyecto de largo aliento que indaga en la memoria y sus vacíos. El título alude tanto a los ecosistemas costeros, sujetos a las fluctuaciones de la marea, como a las ausencias que marcan el recuerdo. Las marcas que el agua deja en la película materializan esa relación entre el entorno y las formas, siempre parciales, de registrar y recordar.

La artista trinitaria Nadia Huggins indaga en la percepción del cuerpo dentro del ecosistema marino a través de la serie de dípticos fotográficos Transformations (2014-2015). El proyecto surgió de sus nados diarios, de la preocupación por el deterioro de los arrecifes de coral y de la sensación de ingravidez que experimentaba al sumergirse.

Cada díptico yuxtapone una imagen del cuerpo de la artista y otra de un animal marino. Entre ambas queda un intervalo que parece a punto de desaparecer, como si ambas imágenes pudieran fundirse en una sola. La transformación ocurre en el espacio que las separa y, a la vez, las aproxima. La mirada oscila allí entre distinguir ambos mundos y percibirlos como parte de una misma continuidad.

La materia que el río arrastra y devuelve conserva las marcas de su recorrido. En teníamos bocas de ceniza (2026), la artista colombiana María Leguízamo parte de una acción colectiva en Punta Roca, donde el Magdalena deposita troncos, raíces, ramas y residuos de origen humano e industrial. A través de conversaciones y de la observación de estos materiales, invita a reunirlos y trasladarlos a la sala de exposición, donde su acumulación evoca un cauce seco. La madera erosionada y los demás restos dan cuenta de las fuerzas que han modelado sus formas —la corriente, los sedimentos, la vibración y el paso del tiempo—, pero también de las actividades humanas, industriales y extractivas.

Christian Salablanca Díaz (Costa Rica, 1990) recurre a la memoria y la transmisión oral en Desbocar un río (2023), parte del proyecto Enciclopedias de Río (Historias Líquidas) . Esta pieza reúne conocimientos compartidos durante recorridos fluviales y costeros, entre ellos los relatos que el artista escuchó de su padre sobre peces, manglares, canoas y prácticas de pesca. Aquí, conocer el río supone recorrerlo, observar sus formas de vida y aprender de quienes han convivido con él. Son saberes que nacen de la experiencia y pasan de una generación a otra.

Lo hidrocomún

La curaduría de Conti propone varios puntos de entrada para comprender la vitalidad del agua desde las cosmogonías y experiencias de comunidades del Caribe, Centroamérica y Sudamérica. Las obras reunidas en Bocas de agua abordan la interdependencia entre los cuerpos humanos y los ecosistemas desde experiencias y conocimientos situados, reconociendo el agua como una presencia activa en la producción de conocimiento y entendiendo que su degradación compromete formas de vida humanas y no humanas.

Bocas de agua invita también a pensar lo hidrocomún: el reconocimiento de que la existencia y el cuidado del agua sostienen formas de vida interdependientes, pero que las responsabilidades y las posibilidades de decidir sobre ella se distribuyen de manera desigual. Pensarla como un bien común exige atender tanto a las relaciones que hacen posible su cuidado como a las estructuras políticas y económicas que condicionan su acceso y explotación.

El título de la muestra adquiere así un sentido que va más allá de la desembocadura como accidente geográfico. Una boca es una abertura por la que circulan el agua, el aire, las palabras y los relatos; una desembocadura, el punto donde distintos cursos confluyen y se transforman. Como parte del programa relay de OtherNetwork, la exposición hace circular historias y saberes entre lugares y comunidades sin borrar las particularidades de cada contexto. Pensar con el agua, como propone Conti, no significa hablar en su nombre, sino atender a las formas de vida, memoria y conocimiento que existen con ella, y a las responsabilidades que esa interdependencia implica.

BOCAS DE AGUA

ASOPLAYA en colaboración con Luis González Vergara, Marilyn Boror Bor, Carolina Caycedo, Seba Calfuqueo, Cheen Chavajay, Manuel Chavajay, davi de jesus do nascimento, Sofía Gallisá Muriente, Regina José Galindo, Nadia Huggins, María Leguízamo, Breidy Manes Robledo, Nomasmetaforas, Christian Salablanca Díaz.

Galería La Escuela , Universidad del Atlántico, Barranquilla, Colombia

Del 15 de octubre al 12 de noviembre de 2026

La exposición se inscribe en la misión de OtherNetwork de fomentar la colaboración transnacional entre espacios de arte independientes. Tras las ediciones realizadas en Stuttgart, Accra, Johannesburgo, Salvador y San Juan, cada una de las cuales puso a prueba las convenciones de las exposiciones itinerantes, «Bocas de agua» se presenta como parte de un programa global que reúne a socios nuevos y existentes en Akosombo, Barranquilla, São Paulo, Santiago y Valdivia. En paralelo, estos espacios desarrollan propuestas que invitan a reflexionar sobre cuestiones vinculadas al hidrofeminismo.

article_text:
On this week’s episode of The Screen Podcast, the team unpacks what this year’s Bifa nominations say about the UK indie film industry at large.

Watch above or listen below

Host Wendy Mitchell is joined by awards and box office editor Charles Gant and UK producer Helen Simmons ( 100 Nights Of Hero, Hoard ) to delve into why the Bifa nominations included so few female filmmakers.

“My worry is that with all the change going on in the industry, the lack of risk that people want to take, what goes out the window first is efforts towards diversity,” Simmons said.

”The only category that was a better showing was debut writer, where it was actually majority women, but I think often it’s about how do female filmmakers have a long career as well? How do they stay in the industry?”

The trio also discussed the wider challenges facing the UK indie sector, including the disappearance of micro-budget features and challenges in the distribution landscape.

To download or subscribe to future episodes, search for ‘The Screen Podcast’, which is available on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , Acast and YouTube .

The Screen Podcast is produced by Ellie Calnan, with Wendy Mitchell serving as editorial director. New episodes every Thursday.

article_text:
The 2027 Karachi Biennale has been cancelled, with the organisers citing in a statement the ‘war conditions prevailing in the regions’. Curated by Noor Ahmed, the fifth edition of the event was due to open for two months from 16 January.

Ahmed had intended the exhibition, titled Kal (Yesterday/Tomorrow), to be ‘a dedication for the hopeful Tomorrow.’

As a key ally of Saudi Arabia, as well as sharing a border with Iran, Pakistan has been drawn into the conflict with Houthi rebels in Yemen.

Ahmed told Pakistan’s Images that she was not consulted on the decision to axe the event, which was ‘devastating for the artists, curators and partners who have devoted so much time and effort in preparing for the Biennale’.

The fourth Lahore Biennale is due to open in March, alongside the 14th general assembly for the International Biennial Association.

article_text:
Art Review

Cannupa Hanska Luger’s Truth About America

The beauty of the Native artist’s forms seduces, but the visual history of destruction is embedded into each element.

Hyperallergic )

Two years ago, I encountered the infamous 1892 image of two men with a hill of buffalo skulls at the Baltimore Museum of Art. It was covered by a small wall-mounted curtain designed by Yurok artist Stormi Turner, and it gave the image, still shocking after over a century of circulation, the depth of tragedy that it warranted. Part of the Preoccupied: Indigenizing the Museum exhibition, it was a way of acknowledging the care that such a crime demands, in the same way that human remains are shown in museums today, often with warnings, behind doors you must open, or under covers that you must actively remove to see. Turner’s intervention was a way to honor an animal that many Native American groups and communities lived in symbiotic relationship with for millennia. That image came back to me when I walked into Cannupa Hanska Luger’s newest exhibition, American Traditional , at Garth Greenan Gallery in Soho, where the artist sets aside the participatory, ceramics-heavy projects he’s best known for and arrives at something more declarative — a synthesis of wood, ink, and archive that is his strongest work yet.

In Mari Sandoz’s The Buffalo Hunters: The Story of the Hide Men , first published in 1954, she explains that North American bison, also called buffalo, were far more numerous than humans on the continent and there was “apparently no disease on all the continent that threatened the buffalo in any number.” That charmed existence for the largest land animal on Turtle Island was interrupted by the eventual arrival of European settlers, who with their horses, guns, and railroads made their slaughter into an industrial-scale activity.

Luger, who was born on the Standing Rock Reservation, places a black abstracted bison atop a blackened rendering of a 19th-century American wood dining table. An enrolled citizen of the Three Affiliated Tribes of the Fort Berthold Reservation, he has deep roots on the Great Plains, and he knows the history of destruction that tore the bison from the tribes of the region that was, as Sandoz put it, “almost the sole subsistence of the Plains Indian — his shelter, clothing, food and fuel.” The Cree scholar Tasha Hubbard goes further than Sandoz was able to. For Plains nations the buffalo were kin, part of the First Peoples rather than a separate species, and the campaign against them was, in her account , a genocide carried out by proxy and a “second major wave of trauma for Plains Indigenous peoples,” after epidemic disease. The army said as much. Hubbard quotes Colonel Richard Irving Dodge’s advice to hunters — “every buffalo dead is an Indian gone” — and General Philip H. Sheridan understood it before the historians did. In 1875, when the Texas legislature proposed a bill to protect the bison, buffalo hunter John R. Cook recorded Sheridan’s objection: “These men [the buffalo hunters] have done more to settle the vexed Indian question than the entire regular army has done in the last thirty years … Send them powder and lead if you will, but for the sake of a lasting peace let them kill, skin and sell until the buffalo are exterminated.”

article_text:
Specialty distributors and alternative fare from live concerts to Indian films to faith-based fare and TV series ruled the top 10 at the box office and beyond this weekend, showcasing the strength of a market that’s helped the box office weather downturns and is now fueling its resurgence.

Godzilla Minus Zero from independent distributor GKids topped the weekend. Angel Studios’ Drummer Boy banged into no. 3, followed by You Can See Everything (A24), Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend (Sony Pictures/Prime Focus Studios), Laika’ animated Wildwood (Fathom Entertainment), Wild Horse Nine (Searchlight Pictures), Stray Kids World Tour ‘RUN IT’ Live Viewing (Trafalgar Entertainment) and Wicker (Black Bear).

Jimmy Stewart biopic Jimmy from Fathom Entertainment and Burns & Co. opened at no. 12 with $2 million at 1,500 theaters.

Watch on Deadline

Heated Rivalry : Regal Entertainment Distribution packaged Episodes 1 and 2 of the popular HBO Max hockey drama to a no. 14 spot with $1.4 million at 945 locations. It will be rolling out more this month.

A24’s Club Kid had one of the best limited openings of the year with $391k on 6 screens. Amazon MGM Studios’ I Play Rocky was strong with $335k from 7 screens. Sony Pictures Classics’ The Only Living Pickpocket in New York is holding well in moderate release with $893k on 818 screens in week 2 for a $3.95 million cume.

Netflix is reporting $975k for La Bola Negra in week 4 at 473 locations, the widest point for the TIFF Audience award winner for a cume of $2.47 million. The Mosquito Bowl grossed $105k in its second week on 309 screens for a $756.4k cume.

NatGeo/Disney nature-adventure doc Everest: The Other Side grossed $320k at 515 locations for a cume of $1.92 million.

Back to Godzilla , which is driving the highest opening weekend box office ever for Gkids after $13 million from The Boy and the Heron (2023). The film’s $31.6+ million domestic debut also makes it the highest grossing opening for a foreign language live action film in North American box office history.

GKids’ distribution VP Chance Huskey said the “landmark release is the result of a thoughtful campaign by GKIDS and Toho that emphasized the ‘must see’ intensity of the theatrical experience and director Takashi Yamazaki’s vision. We’re so happy to see audiences embrace Godzilla Minus Zero at an unprecedented scale for an international film.”

Bollywood’s Ramayana , meanwhile, is the second biggest opening (and the widest release at 1,433 screens) for an Indian movie in North America at $12.2 million (including Thursday previews) behind Dhurandhar: The Revenge , which debuted to $14.5M last March. Separately, Tamil film Scene from Prime Media Pictures opened to $1.28 million at 330 locations.

American Revolution original musical Drummer Boy from Angel and 2521 Entertainment opened to $9.3 million. The film’s music hit #1 on iTunes. The better-than-anticipated take “underscores the strength of audience-driven entertainment and the growing appetite for musicals on the big screen,” the distributor said.

“It has been eight long years of failure and triumph to bring Drummer Boy to the screen,” said co-director and lead actor Joel Smallbone. “To us, this is a story of our own experiences portrayed—a story of ending up on the opposite side of life’s battle-lines, and of forgiveness and freedom and true love. This is a film that’s deeply personal to us. So as you’d imagine I find myself deeply impacted by the fact that this personal story has found its way into hundreds of thousands of your hearts,”

Wild Horse Nine , at $6 million on 1,100 screens, is the best opening weekend for a Martin McDonagh film.

Stray Kids World Tour ‘RUN IT’ Live Viewing from Trafalgar Entertainment — a special live broadcast Saturday from Tokyo Dome to movie theaters worldwide took in $3.7 million on 917 screens in North America.

Wicke r , with $3.5 million on 2,085 screens in week 3, off 23% for a cume of $19.9 million.

As per Rentrak, the domestic marketplace is at an estimated $121.7 million, up 99% week-over-week and 45% year over year. Domestic YTD reaches $8.6 billion, up 21% from 2025.

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "而为了听到鸟鸣", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "战机必须保持沉默。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "——马尔万·马霍尔（Marwan Makhoul）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "搭乘空客A320降落在大开曼岛时，眼前的景象犹如漂浮在广袤加勒比海蓝中的一颗微小而虹彩闪烁的马赛克。环绕整座岛屿的堡垒礁将海水与大海外海隔绝，这里的海水宁静而平缓，微风温暖轻柔。岸边，黄貂鱼平滑如天鹅绒的身影从码头旁滑过，渔民们正在那里甩竿垂钓。沿着通往乔治敦国家美术馆的高速公路，九重葛藤蔓绽放着紫红色与深紫色的繁花，而银叶棕榈高挑挺拔的叶柄则在五颜六色的混凝土房屋上方探出头来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在第四届开曼群岛双年展《群岛》中，对自然世界的崇敬无处不在。各个展馆的墙面上挂满了对该岛独特动植物的描绘：本土的蓝鬣蜥、绿喉与红喉的开曼鹦鹉，以及花瓣状如柠檬皮螺旋的野生香蕉兰。像杰森·肯尼迪（Jason Kennedy）的《红树林》（图1）这样充满田园诗意且技艺精湛的拟真绘画，或许正是你对身处海岛天堂的艺术家之期待，但根系与枝桠所揭示的远不止是美。即使是最精致的自然，也深植于开采、殖民、移民和开发的历史之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "红树林湿地曾是生机勃勃的海洋生物育婴所，也是抵御飓风风暴潮的屏障，如今却为了让高耸的海滨度假村得以在松软的沙滩上奢华享乐而被剥光。转瞬间，肯尼迪的画作不再仅仅是对自然的写生观察。其密不透风、毫无人类影响痕迹的植被，成了对一个正迅速消逝的生态系统的致敬。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-1-300x159.png", "alt": "图1", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "生态系统的转变在伊恩·麦克雷（Iain MacRae）的三联画中得到了最强有力的呈现，画作中充斥着热带物种及其在群岛各处栖息地的地图。豚鼠羞怯的棕色皮毛和海鸟的喙从颜料中隐现，但就连这些开曼群岛的经典标志也并非岛上的本土物种。外来物种（其中既有入侵物种，也有农业物种）与本土生物在画布上激烈交织，而在它们之中隐隐透出象征性醒目的则是进口、金融和房地产公司的标志。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-2.-291x300.png", "alt": "图2", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "开曼群岛的艺术家深知自然无法与政治绝缘。联合策展人同样深谙此道。达温·K·埃班克斯（Davin K. Ebanks）和约瑟夫·L·安德伍德（Joseph L. Underwood）提供了三个概念视角，借此审视分布在3个岛屿共6个场馆中的76件艺术品：文化转型、社会动态与生态遗产。这些子主题相互交织、重叠，每一条都是一条曲折的小径，最终通往双年展的核心前提——同名主题《群岛》。岛屿的集合、文化的集合、人群的集合：群岛既是孤立的，又是紧密相连的。移民、现代化和不断扩张的旅游业彻底重塑了岛屿生活。而这反过来又重塑了土地、海洋以及栖息在那里的所有生物。一些艺术家在与乡愁博弈，例如纳萨里娅·苏库·乔利特（Nasaria Suckoo Chollette），她用精细的纺织品和现成品创作的祖母肖像，勾起了人们对逝去记忆和不再代代相传的生活方式的回忆（图3）。一些艺术作品则对未来感到恐惧，例如凯·史密斯（Kay Smith）的拼贴画，画中一名戴着防毒面具的年轻女性穿行于大开曼岛臭名昭著的垃圾填埋场“拉什莫尔山”（Mount Rashmore）（图4）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在无休无止的垃圾洪流之外，一座原始的宅邸被封存在玻璃雪景球中——这是面向旅游驱动型经济的完美纪念品伴手礼。一些艺术作品则在构筑梦想，例如约尼耶·鲍威瑞（Yonier Powery）的陶瓷雕塑《坚韧》（图5）。一只手工雕刻的乌龟背负着一座饱经风吹雨打的房屋。神话般超现实的动物似乎正处于无休止的迁徙状态。或许群岛中的这座岛屿将成为它的家，又或许是下一座。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-3.-185x300.png", "alt": "图3", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-4-300x221.png", "alt": "图4", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-5.-218x300.png", "alt": "图5", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "双年展中最具力量的一些艺术作品隐匿于画廊墙壁之外。在一处名为格拉姆贝拉（Gram Bella’s）的前杂货铺混凝土废墟中，一座巨大的装置艺术在天空下徐徐展开。艺术家斯特凡·朗卢瓦（Stefan Langlois）和伊丽莎白·佩奇·史密斯（Elizabeth Paige Smith）用幽灵般的形象填满了这座老建筑。高耸的雕刻木质船桅从泥土中拔地而起，出现在《致十帆船之歌》（图6）中——这是朗卢瓦对1794年十帆船失事事件的戏剧化诠释，当时一支英国船队撞上了暗礁。它们像防御栅栏一样从商店空洞的立面中向外碎裂开来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些雕塑造型宏伟、制作精巧，既像是一座纪念碑，又像是一个警告。毕竟，只有幸存者才能讲述过去的故事。在废墟深处，史密斯留下了一组静止的人物编舞。《属于它且源于其中》（图 7）是这些角色中体量最大的一件：一个由铸造开曼白云石制成的庞大化石身躯。她的皮肤层层叠叠地镶嵌着珊瑚、骨螺和生锈的金属，宛如藤壶一般。谁也不知道她已经在那里躺了多久，但这种堆积表明她年代久远。格拉姆·贝拉（Gram Bella）杂货店里的这件装置艺术，既关乎开曼人民的韧性，也关乎人类对群岛地貌造成的永久性影响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-6-300x254.png", "alt": "图 6", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-7-226x300.jpg", "alt": "图 7", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《群岛》是一个名副其实的展览；这里的艺术家们依然如同其海洋先辈一般，在汹涌的加勒比海域中穿行。面对过度旅游与过度开发带来的生态威胁，当生态系统和记忆一同侵蚀入海时，他们依然在创作。开曼群岛当代艺术界的爆发，似乎映照出自1970年代以来其工业和人口的爆发。珍妮特·沃克（Janet Walker）等艺术家的作品点缀着国家美术馆常设展厅的墙壁，那是他们在60年代和70年代创作的、洒满阳光的棕榈树和吊床水彩画。而双年展上展出的作品则根本不同：它们更具关切意识、更具批判性、也更具政治性。当我联系策展人询问为什么这些当代艺术家会让人感到如此激进时，达文·K·埃班克斯（Davin K. Ebanks）对“本土之子”（Native Sons）给予了极高的评价——这是一个艺术集体，其成员自90年代以来一直在推动艺术界的专业化。他们在规模和媒介上都极具雄心，对岛屿独特的社会文化体验有着敏锐的洞察力，其成员在开曼群岛双年展的许多往届活动中都备受瞩目。埃班克斯还赞扬了由娜塔莉·厄克特（Natalie Urquhart）领导的国家美术馆的领导层，她重塑了人们对艺术界的期待。通过推行公开征集、吸引拥有艺术硕士（MFA）学历的艺术家、策展人和研究人员，美术馆树立了新的标准，而双年展正是其中一个面向。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "许多这类艺术家描绘了自然的当代处境，并意识到他们有责任超越那些假装天堂一切安好的甜腻棕榈树画作。双年展的艺术与我老家纽约市的生态艺术界之间，有着许多概念上的平行呼应。2025年，纽约布鲁克林的生物蝙蝠艺术空间（BioBat Art Space）迎来了宏大的艺术与生态展《水之故事》（Water Stories）。《水之故事》的核心叙事之一是，地球上已不存在未遭触及的纯粹自然。核沉降物在海洋海沟最深超深渊带（hadal zone）隐隐阴燃。微塑料漂浮在高积云中，并随着降水落下。人类对地球的影响在规模上是地质的、气象的和宇宙级的。《水之故事》将科学视为我们获得救赎的工具，而《群岛》则将目光投向彼此。这里有着对彼此依赖的敏锐觉察，呼吁建立社群与问责机制，并为子孙后代保护土地及其遗产。街头艺术家喜鹊（Magpie）在所有三个岛屿上都留下了喷漆标志，非常坦率地提出了这样一个问题：“这值多少钱？”（图 8）画面描绘了一对海龟和一个称量成堆货币的天平，给人一种感觉：如果可以的话，喜鹊会用这种涂鸦标记每一个政府建筑和企业办公室。随着岛屿生活继续经历急剧变革，个体与集体都负有责任。喜鹊提醒了我们这一点，并坚持认为开曼人民应当继续分享他们的故事。\\n\\n《群岛》成为了一个放大这些故事并将其置于新语境中的框架，从一个岛屿跃向另一个岛屿，从一个城镇跃向另一个城镇，从一个灵魂跃向另一个灵魂。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-8-300x295.png", "alt": "图 8", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.9.jpg", "alt": "Fig.9", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Archipelago is an exhibition that lives up to its title; its artists still navigate the restless Caribbean waters much like their maritime ancestors. They create in the face of ecological threats from overtourism and overdevelopment, as both ecosystems and memories erode into the sea."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Between Mangroves and Excavators"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Reflections on the Art of the 4 th Cayman Islands Biennial"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In order for me to write poetry that isn’ t political"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I must listen to the birds"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "and in order to hear the birds"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "the warplanes must be silent."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "– Marwan Makhoul"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Descending onto Grand Cayman in an airbus A320, the view is of a tiny, iridescent mosaic floating in the vast Caribbean blue. Shielded from the sea by a barrier reef that embraces the entire island, the waters are serene and still; the wind is warm and gentle. On the shore, the smooth, velvet shapes of stingrays slip past the docks where fisherman cast and reel. Along the highway to the National Gallery in George Town, bougainvillea vines exuberate in fuchsia and violet, while the tall bristling masts of silver thatch palms peer over the colorful concrete houses."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In Archipelago , the 4th edition of the Cayman Islands Biennial, there is no shortage of reverence for the natural world. Depictions of the islands’ unique flora and fauna fill the walls of the various venues: the native blue iguana, the green and red-throated Cayman parrots, wild banana orchids with their petals like spirals of lemon zest. The idyllic and masterful mimesis in paintings such as Jason Kennedy’s Mangroves (Fig. 1) may be what you expect of an artist creating in an island paradise, but roots and branches reveal more than beauty. Even the most exquisite nature is embedded within histories of extraction, colonization, immigration, and development."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The mangrove wetlands themselves, once thriving nurseries of marine life and a bulwark from the storm surges of hurricanes, have been denuded so that towering seaside resorts can luxuriate along the soft sand beaches. Suddenly Kennedy’s painting becomes more than a plein air observation of nature. Its dense, impenetrable vegetation, with no trace of human impact, is a tribute to a rapidly disappearing ecosystem."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-1-300x159.png", "alt": "Fig. 1", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The transforming of ecosystems is perhaps most assertively represented in Iain MacRae’s triptych paintings teem with tropical species, cartography of their habitats across the Islands. The shy brown fur of the agouti and the beaks of seabirds emerge in fragments from the paint, but even these classic Cayman icons are not endemic to the islands. Introduced species, some invasive, some agricultural, wrestle across the canvas with the native organisms, and looming amongst them all in emblematic boldness are the logos of import, finance, and real estate corporations."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-2.-291x300.png", "alt": "Fig. 2.", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The artists of the Cayman Islands know that nature cannot be insulated from the political. And the co-curators know this as well. Davin K. Ebanks and Joseph L. Underwood have offered three conceptual lenses through which to view the 76 artworks across 6 venues and 3 islands: Culture Shift, Social Dynamics, and Ecological Legacies. These subthemes overlap and intertwine, each a meandering footpath leading back to the biennial’s overarching premise, the titular, “ Archipelago .” A collection of islands, a collection of cultures, a collection of people: an archipelago is simultaneously isolated and vitally interconnected. Migration, modernization, and a proliferating tourism industry have completely reshaped island life. This, in turn, has reshaped the land, the sea, and all the creatures that dwell there. Some artists contend with nostalgia, like Nasaria Suckoo Chollette, whose sensitive textile and found object portrait of her grandmother hearkens to memories lost and a way of life no longer passed down (Fig. 3). Some artworks fear for the future, like Kay Smith’s collage were a young woman in a gas mask makes her way through Grand Cayman’s notorious landfill “Mount Rashmore.” (Fig. 4)."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Beyond the endless flood of garbage, apristine mansion is encased in a glass snow globe—the perfect trinket takeaway for a tourist-driven economy. Some artworks dream, like Yonier Powery’s ceramic sculpture Resilient (Fig. 5). A hand sculpted tortoise carries a windswept house on its back. Mythological and surreal, the animal appears to be in a state of endless migration. Perhaps this island in the archipelago will be its home, or perhaps the next one."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-3.-185x300.png", "alt": "Fig. 3.", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-4-300x221.png", "alt": "Fig. 4", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://africanah.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Fig.-5.-218x300.png", "alt": "Fig. 5.", "caption": "", "credit": "Africanah.org"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Some of the biennial’s most powerful artworks lie beyond the gallery walls. Enclosed within the concrete ruins of a former grocery called Gram Bella’s, a monumental installation unfurls beneath the sky. Artists Stefan Langlois and Elizabeth Paige Smith have inhabited the old structure with ghostly figures. Tall carved wooden ship masts jut from the earth in Ode to Ten (Fig. 6), Langlois’ dramatic interpretation of the 1794 Wreck of the Ten Sail, when a fleet of British ships crashed into the reef. They shatter outwards like palisade fortifications from the hollow façade of the store."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Imposing in form and deft in fabrication, the sculptures seem like both a memorial and a warning. It is after all, only the survivors who get to tell the stories of the past. Deeper within the ruins, Smith has left a choreography of figures in repose. In It and Of It (Fig. 7) is the title of the largest of these characters: a vast fossilized body made of cast Cayman Dolostone. article_text:
Archipelago is an exhibition that lives up to its title; its artists still navigate the restless Caribbean waters much like their maritime ancestors. They create in the face of ecological threats from overtourism and overdevelopment, as both ecosystems and memories erode into the sea.

Between Mangroves and Excavators

Reflections on the Art of the 4 th Cayman Islands Biennial

In order for me to write poetry that isn’ t political

I must listen to the birds

and in order to hear the birds

the warplanes must be silent.

– Marwan Makhoul

Descending onto Grand Cayman in an airbus A320, the view is of a tiny, iridescent mosaic floating in the vast Caribbean blue. Shielded from the sea by a barrier reef that embraces the entire island, the waters are serene and still; the wind is warm and gentle. On the shore, the smooth, velvet shapes of stingrays slip past the docks where fisherman cast and reel. Along the highway to the National Gallery in George Town, bougainvillea vines exuberate in fuchsia and violet, while the tall bristling masts of silver thatch palms peer over the colorful concrete houses.

In Archipelago , the 4th edition of the Cayman Islands Biennial, there is no shortage of reverence for the natural world. Depictions of the islands’ unique flora and fauna fill the walls of the various venues: the native blue iguana, the green and red-throated Cayman parrots, wild banana orchids with their petals like spirals of lemon zest. The idyllic and masterful mimesis in paintings such as Jason Kennedy’s Mangroves (Fig. 1) may be what you expect of an artist creating in an island paradise, but roots and branches reveal more than beauty. Even the most exquisite nature is embedded within histories of extraction, colonization, immigration, and development.

The mangrove wetlands themselves, once thriving nurseries of marine life and a bulwark from the storm surges of hurricanes, have been denuded so that towering seaside resorts can luxuriate along the soft sand beaches. Suddenly Kennedy’s painting becomes more than a plein air observation of nature. Its dense, impenetrable vegetation, with no trace of human impact, is a tribute to a rapidly disappearing ecosystem.

The transforming of ecosystems is perhaps most assertively represented in Iain MacRae’s triptych paintings teem with tropical species, cartography of their habitats across the Islands. The shy brown fur of the agouti and the beaks of seabirds emerge in fragments from the paint, but even these classic Cayman icons are not endemic to the islands. Introduced species, some invasive, some agricultural, wrestle across the canvas with the native organisms, and looming amongst them all in emblematic boldness are the logos of import, finance, and real estate corporations.

The artists of the Cayman Islands know that nature cannot be insulated from the political. And the co-curators know this as well. Davin K. Ebanks and Joseph L. Underwood have offered three conceptual lenses through which to view the 76 artworks across 6 venues and 3 islands: Culture Shift, Social Dynamics, and Ecological Legacies. These subthemes overlap and intertwine, each a meandering footpath leading back to the biennial’s overarching premise, the titular, “ Archipelago .” A collection of islands, a collection of cultures, a collection of people: an archipelago is simultaneously isolated and vitally interconnected. Migration, modernization, and a proliferating tourism industry have completely reshaped island life. This, in turn, has reshaped the land, the sea, and all the creatures that dwell there. Some artists contend with nostalgia, like Nasaria Suckoo Chollette, whose sensitive textile and found object portrait of her grandmother hearkens to memories lost and a way of life no longer passed down (Fig. 3). Some artworks fear for the future, like Kay Smith’s collage were a young woman in a gas mask makes her way through Grand Cayman’s notorious landfill “Mount Rashmore.” (Fig. 4).

Beyond the endless flood of garbage, apristine mansion is encased in a glass snow globe—the perfect trinket takeaway for a tourist-driven economy. Some artworks dream, like Yonier Powery’s ceramic sculpture Resilient (Fig. 5). A hand sculpted tortoise carries a windswept house on its back. Mythological and surreal, the animal appears to be in a state of endless migration. Perhaps this island in the archipelago will be its home, or perhaps the next one.

Some of the biennial’s most powerful artworks lie beyond the gallery walls. Enclosed within the concrete ruins of a former grocery called Gram Bella’s, a monumental installation unfurls beneath the sky. Artists Stefan Langlois and Elizabeth Paige Smith have inhabited the old structure with ghostly figures. Tall carved wooden ship masts jut from the earth in Ode to Ten (Fig. 6), Langlois’ dramatic interpretation of the 1794 Wreck of the Ten Sail, when a fleet of British ships crashed into the reef. They shatter outwards like palisade fortifications from the hollow façade of the store.

Imposing in form and deft in fabrication, the sculptures seem like both a memorial and a warning. It is after all, only the survivors who get to tell the stories of the past. Deeper within the ruins, Smith has left a choreography of figures in repose. In It and Of It (Fig. 7) is the title of the largest of these characters: a vast fossilized body made of cast Cayman Dolostone. Embedded like barnacles, her skin is layered with coral, onch shells, and rusty metal. Who knows how long she has lain there, but this accretion suggests she is ancient. The installation at Gram Bella’s is as much about the resilience of the Caymanian people as it is about the permanent impact that humans have had on the landscape of the islands.

Archipelago is an exhibition that lives up to its title; its artists still navigate the restless Caribbean waters much like their maritime ancestors. They create in the face of ecological threats from overtourism and overdevelopment, as both ecosystems and memories erode into the sea. The explosion of the Cayman Islands’ contemporary art scene seems to mirror the explosion of their industries and population since the 1970’s. Artists like Janet Walker grace the walls of the permanent collection in the National Gallery with sundrenched watercolors of palm trees and hammocks, painted in the 60s and 70s. The work exhibited in the biennial is fundamentally different: more concerned, more critical, more political. When I reached out to the curators asking about why these contemporary artists feel so radical, Davin K. Ebanks gave plenty of credit to the Native Sons, an art collective whose members have professionalized the art scene since the 90s. Ambitious in scale and medium, with delicate discernment for what makes the socio-cultural experience of their islands so unique, their members have been highlighted in many prior editions of the Cayman Islands Biennial. Ebanks also praised the leadership of the National Gallery, directed by Natalie Urquhart, who has transformed the expectations of the art scene. Implementing open calls, drawing in artists with MFAs, curators, and researchers; this has set a new standard which the biennial is one facet of.

Many of these artists depict the contemporary conditions of nature and recognize the responsibility they have to go beyond the saccarine palm tree paintings feigning that all is well in paradise. There are many conceptual parallels between the art of the biennial and the eco-art scene in my home, New York City. 2025 saw the towering art and ecology showcase Water Stories , at BioBat Art Space in Brooklyn, NYC. One of the core storylines of Water Stories was that there is no wild, untouched nature left on earth. Nuclear fallout smolders in the deepest hadal zones of oceanic trenches. Microplastics float in cirrus clouds and fall in precipitation. The human impact on earth has been geological, meteorological, and cosmic in scale. While Water Stories looked to science as the tool of our salvation, Archipelago looks to each other. There is a keen awareness of our dependency on one another, calling for community and accountability, and preserving the land and its heritage for future generations. The graffiti artist Magpie very candidly asks this question, with a spraypainted emblem included on all three islands: “ What is it Worth?” (Fig. 8) Illustrating a pair of sea turtles and a scale weighing stacks of currency, there is a sense that if he could, Magpie would tag every government building and corporate office with this graffiti. There is both individual and collective responsibility as island life continues to undergo rapid transformations. Magpie reminds us of this, and he insists that Caymanian people continue to share their stories. Archipelago becomes a framework to amplify these stories and place them in new contexts, bounding from island to island, from town to town, and from soul to soul.

日曜日の散歩者 わすれられた台湾詩人たち

劇場公開日： 2026年10月15日

予告編を見る

U-NEXTで 関連作品を見る PR

解説・あらすじ

1933年日本統治下の台湾に登場したモダニズム詩人団体にスポットを当てたドキュメンタリーで、台湾のアカデミー賞に相当する金馬奨で最優秀ドキュメンタリー賞を受賞。 日本による植民地支配が40年近く経過した1930年代の台湾で誕生したモダニズム詩人団体「風車詩社」。植民地支配下で日本語教育を受け、日本留学の経験を持つ彼らエリートは、日本語による詩を創作し、新しい台湾文学の創造を試みた。日本近代詩の先駆者で、世界的評価を得ているモダニストの西脇順三郎や瀧口修造といった日本文学者たちから刺激を受け、ジャン・コクトーなどの西洋モダニズム文学に触れ、情熱を育んでいった若きシュルレアリストたちが、二二八事件、白色テロといった時代のうねりに巻き込まれていく。1年半で活動を終え、歴史に埋もれた「風車詩社」の文学を通し、当時の台湾と日本の関係や、政治弾圧という社会的な側面が浮かび上がらせていく。

News

Art Basel Paris Undergoes Lockdown Ahead of Opening

Police ordered the Grand Palais to briefly shut down amid the nationwide student protests.

The Grand Palais in Paris went into temporary lockdown during installation for Art Basel Paris on Saturday, October 17, amid nearby protests over France’s education system and public services, a fair representative confirmed to Hyperallergic .

The Paris Police Prefecture ordered the Grand Palais — which has housed Art Basel Paris since 2024, two years after the Swiss art fair network replaced the exhibition hall's longstanding FIAC (Foire Internationale d'Art Contemporain) — to briefly shut down to “ensure the safety of everyone on site and the protection of the artworks,” an Art Basel spokesperson told Hyperallergic . The lockdown occurred at 5 pm, and the building sustained no damage, another fair spokesperson said.

"No one could get out, and no one could get in," an anonymous source from a New York gallery exhibiting at the fair told Hyperallergic. "There were moving trucks loading and offloading works, and at a certain point, they were told to pack up and go."

article_text:
Artículos

Melissa Benoist da un brinco de Glee a Supergirl

Julio Vélez

CBS y productores de la nueva serie de TV anuncian a la nueva Supergirl. Melissa Benoist salta de Glee al papel de la prima de Superman. ¿Complacidos?

Cuando se trata de encarnar a los superhéroes con los que crecimos, es inevitable que surjan miles de preguntas sobre quién será la persona que pueda cumplir con las características y aptitudes imposibles de estos personajes. Supergirl no es la excepción. El cuestionamiento sobre quién sería perfecta para interpretarla no cesa, por eso es que no podemos pasar por alto el hecho de que CBS informara recientemente que Melissa Benoist, de Whiplash (2014), tendrá el estelar en la nueva serie de superhéroes.

Curiosamente, Benoist proviene de la misma serie de donde Grant Gustin surgió para interpretar a Flash : Glee . Pero también podrán ver su talento actoral en Whiplash: Música y obsesión , una de las películas multinominadas a los premios Oscar.

Benoist interpretará en la serie a Kara Zor-El, prima sanguínea de Kal-El, aunque se ignora si Superman tendrá presencia en la serie. Ya en el planeta Tierra y con 24 años cumplidos, la kriptoniana decidirá usar sus poderes y habilidades como la heroína que siempre fue destinada a ser.

Por cierto, minutos después del anuncio oficial, Benoist expresó su emoción en Twitter, y los “superhéroes” Stephen Amell ( Arrow ) y Gustin la felicitaron (¿se imaginan ya un crossover con los 3?). ¡Bienvenida al universo DC en la TV!

¿Qué les parece esta elección?

Julio Vélez Colaborador en web y revista Cine PREMIERE desde 2006. Me especializo en anime/manga, comics, doblaje, tecnología y videojuegos. Mis sagas favoritas: Doctor Who, Star Trek, Dragon Ball y Star Wars. Batimaníaco, geek ochentero y hardcore gamer.

article_text:
Several films—both old and new—across this year’s NYFF lineup push the boundaries of depictions of sensuality and desire on screen, posing provocative questions for the current cinema landscape, where sex has become a divisive subject.

Last Tuesday at the festival, filmmaker and scholar Ayanna Dozier and Film Comment Contributing Editor Melissa Anderson joined F ilm Comment Editors Devika Girish and Clinton Krute to explore films like Nitrate Kisses , The Devils , The Drift , The Unknown , and others to discuss what thrills and terrifies us about sexuality on screen.

This episode is sponsored by Criterion .

article_text:
Turkish authorities have seized a marble head depicting the ancient Greek god Zeus in Izmir’s Konak district in western Turkey. The sculpture, which is believed to date to the Roman period around 2,000 years ago, was recovered during an operation conducted by the İzmir Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office with officers from the Anti-Smuggling and Intelligence branches of the provincial police department.

Three unnamed suspects were detained in the course of the operation and charged with violating Turkey’s Law No. 2863 on the Protection of Cultural and Natural Heritage. According to the Turkish news agency Demirören , the three were arrested after appearing in court.

Authorities have not revealed how the suspects acquired the sculpture, or whether it can be associated with a known archaeological site, illustrating the difficulties of establishing the age and historical significance of looted artifacts.

As ruler of the Olympian gods, Zeus occupied a central position in Greek mythology; following Rome’s conquest of Greece, he became associated with the Roman god Jupiter while continuing to be depicted according to classical sculptural conventions. His cult was widespread in ancient Anatolia throughout the Greek, Hellenistic, and Roman periods.

For now, a more complete picture of the sculpture’s age and origins is pending.

article_text:
After 17 years of leadership, Bob Daly will step down as chair of the American Film Institute Board of Directors at the next trustee meeting on Wednesday, Oct. 21, Variety can reveal exclusively.

Daly, former Warner Bros. chair and co-CEO, joined the AFI Board in April 1981 and was named chair on Oct. 8, 2009, succeeding co-chairs Jon Avnet and John Cooke.

“In a career that brought me from running CBS to Warner Bros. to the Los Angeles Dodgers, I can honestly say that serving as Chairman of the AFI Board of Directors has been one of the greatest honors of my life,” said Daly. “This is a board that represents all aspects of the film and television communities, and to see they come together with a shared passion for the art form has been a wonder to behold. Long live the AFI!”

Related Stories

Documentary Festival IDFA to Open With 'White Tiger Column,' Following Rookie Resistance Fighters in Myanmar

‘Big Boys Don’t Cry’ Director Muhammad Mustapha Talks Masculinity Ahead of El Gouna Premiere: ‘The Only Emotion Men Are Allowed to Express Is Anger’

Daly’s expansive history in Hollywood touched some of the most powerful institutions in the entertainment business, including CBS Entertainment, Warner Music Group, the Los Angeles Dodgers and, of course, Warner Bros. He began his career at CBS as a gofer in 1955. He spent 25 years at the network and eventually served as its president, overseeing all television operations. After his time at CBS, Daly joined Warner Bros. as chairman and co-CEO in 1980. During his 19 years at the studio, he and his co-CEO, Terry Semel, were credited with 16 consecutive years of record earnings. They also supervised the release of 13 Best Picture Oscar nominees, and snagged three wins with “Chariots of Fire,” “Driving Miss Daisy” and “Unforgiven.”

Following his time at WB, Daly joined the Los Angeles Dodgers as chair and CEO for four years before selling the team in 2004. Daly also served as chair of the charity Save the Children.

“Leadership is an art in itself — and in that regard, Mr. Daly is a master,” said Bob Gazzale, AFI president & CEO. “Over the past forty years, no single person has had a greater impact on AFI’s work in preservation, celebration and education than Bob Daly — and we have promised to march forward each day with a promise to prove him proud.”

The AFI, founded in 1967, is a nonprofit organization created to preserve the heritage of the motion picture, to honor the artists and their work and to educate the next generation of storytellers. Former Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy serves as chair of the AFI Board of Trustees, which includes Avnet, Pam Abdy, Sean Astin, Alan Bergman, Halle Berry, Jim Breyer, James L. Brooks, Ava DuVernay, Jamie Erlicht, Rich Frank, Mike Hopkins, Alan Horn, Patty Jenkins, Michael B. Jordan, Donna Langley, Eva Longoria, Bryan Lourd, Christopher Nolan, Edward James Olmos, Shonda Rhimes, Charles Rivkin, Jay Roach, Ted Sarandos, Chris Silbermann, Octavia Spencer, Steven Spielberg, Todd Wagner and Edward Zwick.
